svg.text: Karp's four steps of access control, with every component placed under the step it performs — and, below, the three axes that cut across all of them.
the right to use an identity
writes name ← K · who may write it, for how long
needed only when the check needs a name
hosts — DNS name, Web PKI, CT, ACME
one lens — who writes the binding, and for how long
the subject — TLS, passkey, mTLS, DPoP
or the artifact itself — a bearer string
is its own credential, if it stays secret
copy it and you have copied the authority
cryptography gets you this far and no further
an OAuth consent screen is a PAP
policy decision point — must be correct
OAuth authorization server · ZTA policy engine
bind to a holder, scope, attenuate, expire
ZTA policy administrator · Flask cache + revocation
the thing whose authority is in question
only this box needs the topology property
OAuth resource server · Flask object manager · LSM hook
kernel handle table · capability gateway · tool-call policy
PEPs stack, and each layer fails differently
a peer, a parent, whoever already holds it
hands on a reference — strictly less than it holds
no PDP, no store, no round trip, nobody informed
WHERE · in whose domain the decision is made
resource owner's domain — presigned URL, OAuth token
subject's domain — ZBAC, ocap delegation, attenuation
"shift left" is a claim about when; cross-organizational scale comes from where.
decide in advance, carry the answer — OAuth, presigned URLs, Kerberos tickets
decide at request time, every time — XACML, AuthZEN, Flask's security server
no decision plane at all — a holder hands on a reference. Only the PEP survives.
WHEN · how much of the decision the artifact already carries
work moves from request time to issue time →

g.text: most of the decision is made

svg.text: DESIGNATION · the axis the ladder cannot see

Every rung above is a claim presented to a verifier. Attenuation moves you right along it; it never changes the axis. This is what does — and it is the real difference between a macaroon and a capability.
token · scope · macaroon · JWT · ACL entry
ACL check · token verify · resource server
or not she may use it, so the
every rung of the ladder lands
authority are one act, so it
no PDP left to ask, which is
why it can be small enough to verify
every edge was handed over, once
WHY NO VERSION OF OAUTH COULD CLOSE THE GAP

A scope is a coarse label on an impersonation, not an attenuation of an authority. Closing that needs a way for the delegate to reach one object and nothing else — and no delegation protocol touches communication.
